params.body:
## Why

Testing Mollie on staging, the day before the production cutover, with `mollie` in `OUTBOUND_IMPACT` and a valid test key:

```
✗ mollie  Illuminate\Http\Client\StrayRequestException: Attempted request to [https://api.mollie.com/v2/methods] without a matching fake.
```

The seal refused a service that was explicitly allowed.

## The empty pattern list

`Outbound::services()` listed `'mollie' => ['impact' => []]` with the comment "Mollie belt via zijn SDK (Guzzle), dus alleen de code-bewaking telt". That is no longer true: `mollie/laravel-mollie` ships `Mollie\Laravel\MollieLaravelHttpClientAdapter`, which puts the SDK on Laravel's `Http` facade. So `preventStrayRequests()` sees every Mollie call, and with no pattern there is no passage — the allow-list is the only door, and the code guard in `MollieService` cannot open it.

Mollie now carries `https://api.mollie.com/*`. That is the only host it reaches: `MollieApiClient::API_ENDPOINT` and, for Mollie Connect, `MollieConnectProvider`'s token URL `https://api.mollie.com/oauth2/tokens` (the `www.mollie.com` checkout and authorize URLs are browser redirects, not calls of ours). The code guard stays next to it: it says *why* something is refused, in Dutch, instead of an exception out of the HTTP client.

## Which other services share it

Every remaining empty list was checked against how the service actually travels:

| Service | Empty list | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `mail` | `impact: []` | Correct. Mail goes through the mailer, not the HTTP client; the seal puts `mail.default` on `log` (seal step 1) unless both locks of `mailOpen()` are open. A URL pattern would mean nothing here. |
| `webhooks` | `impact: []` | Correct. The partner's webhook URL only exists in the database at call time; `Outbound::allowUrl()` opens that one address per call, after `impact('webhooks')` said yes. |
| `nederlandmobiel` | `impact: []` | Correct. `OwnStockService` calls `https://www.nederlandmobiel.nl/extern/save_vehicle.php` with raw cURL, invisible to the HTTP client; the code guard is the only guard there, and it is in place. |
| `mollie` | `impact: []` | **Wrong** — the bug above. |

`carpass`, `whatsapp`, `removebg`, `blurit`, `openai`, `realgarant`, `flexlease` and `vwe` all carry patterns already (`realgarant`, `flexlease` and `blurit` derive theirs from configuration, and `hasAddress()` already turns a missing address into "off" instead of a 500). A test now pins the set of pattern-less services to exactly `mail`, `nederlandmobiel` and `webhooks`, so the next empty list is a decision rather than an oversight.

Two smaller repairs found next to it, same failure mode (an allowed service ends up blocked):

- `Outbound::allowUrl()` called `Http::allowStrayRequests([$url])`, and that method **replaces** the factory's list rather than appending. One outgoing webhook therefore closed every other service for the rest of the request. It now merges with `allowedPatterns()`.
- `seal()` only set the list when it was non-empty, leaving a stale list from an earlier seal in place. It now always sets it, empty included.

## What the error says now

`Outbound::sealRefusal($url)` turns a refusal into one sentence that names the host, the service the catalogue knows at that host, and which of the two reasons applies:

- not listed: `de seal liet api.mollie.com niet door (mollie); staat mollie in OUTBOUND_ALLOW of OUTBOUND_IMPACT?`
- listed but no pattern covers the address: `... (realgarant); realgarant staat wel in de lijst, maar geen enkel patroon in Outbound::services() dekt dit adres.`
- host unknown to the catalogue: `... geen dienst in Outbound::services() kent dit adres.`

A catch-all fake inside `seal()` was considered and rejected: the stub handler runs before the stray check, and a global middleware would fire before `Http::fake()` in every test, so either one would break faking. Instead `stocklist:smoke` catches `StrayRequestException` and prints that sentence, and any other caller can do the same in one line.

## Checked

- `php artisan test --filter='Outbound|IntegrationSmoke|Smoke|Mollie|RulesCoverage'` — 153 tests green, own MySQL database loaded from `database/schema/mysql-schema.sql` plus the post-2026-07-28 migrations, the way CI does, and dropped afterwards.
- New tests: Mollie passes the seal when allowed and no other host does; nothing passes when it is not listed; only services that bypass the HTTP client may have an empty pattern list; one webhook URL keeps the other services open; the refusal sentence names the service and the reason; `stocklist:smoke` reads the payment methods through the seal (faked) and translates a refusal instead of printing "without a matching fake". No test makes a real call.
- The full suite has 7 pre-existing failures in this worktree only, all from generated front-end assets that are not committed (`public/js/vehicle/create.js`, the build stamp); CI builds those before the tests.
- Rule `R P3-7.8` added to `docs/bedrijfsregels/33-p3-integraties.md` (P3-7, environment and outgoing traffic): a service that travels through the platform's HTTP layer needs its addresses in the catalogue, an empty list means another channel, and a refusal says which service and why. `92-testdekking.md` and `docs/bedrijfsregels.html` regenerated with `bin/rules-coverage --write` and `bin/rules-page`.
params.title: Outbound: Mollie passes the seal when it is allowed
